# Reverse Polarity
## Step 1 — Split the binary into 8-bit groups

Take:

01000011 01010100 01000110 01111011
01000010 01101001 01110100 01011111
01000110 01101100 01101001 01110000
01110000 01101001 01101110 01111101

Each group is 8 bits = 1 byte.

## Step 2 — Convert each byte to ASCII

For example:

01000011 = 67 = C
01010100 = 84 = T
01000110 = 70 = F
01111011 = 123 = {

Continuing:

01000010 = B
01101001 = i
01110100 = t
01011111 = _
01000110 = F
01101100 = l
01101001 = i
01110000 = p
01110000 = p
01101001 = i
01101110 = n
01111101 = }

You can do the same quickly in Kali with:
```bash
echo '01000011010101000100011001111011010000100110100101110100010111110100011001101100011010010111000001110000011010010110111001111101' | perl -lpe '$_=pack"B*",$_'
```
So the decoded text is the ✅ Flag:
```bash
CTF{Bit_Flippin}
```
